title: AIIA Clinical Trials Dashboard - a real-time, cloud-based, GCP-compliant Clinical Trial Management System (CTMS) for Ayurveda research, with CDISC/FHIR-interoperable data, role-based KPIs, and integrated ethics, regulatory (CTRI / NDCT Rules 2019) and pharmacovigilance tracking.
dataset_link:
Clinical-trial data is sensitive personal data, so development should use synthetic / de-identified datasets; representative standards and public sources:

• Clinical Trials Registry – India (public trial records) - ctri.nic.in
• CDISC standards & controlled terminology (CDASH, SDTM, ADaM, Define-XML) - cdisc.org

description:
Background:
The All India Institute of Ayurveda (AIIA) conducts and coordinates a growing portfolio of clinical research in Ayurveda - interventional and observational studies, multi-centre trials - and, as the host of the National Pharmacovigilance Coordination Centre (NPvCC) for ASU&H drugs, it also anchors nationwide safety surveillance. This activity is governed by a demanding compliance framework: mandatory prospective registration in the Clinical Trials Registry – India (CTRI); the Good Clinical Practice guidelines for ASU medicine (GCP-ASU) and the ICMR National Ethical Guidelines; the New Drugs and Clinical Trials Rules, 2019 where applicable; Institutional Ethics Committee oversight; and timely Adverse-Event / Serious-Adverse-Event reporting. Yet study status, recruitment, milestones, data quality and safety signals are typically tracked across spreadsheets and disconnected tools, with no single, real-time, auditable view. The result is delayed decisions, missed reporting timelines and avoidable compliance risk - precisely as Ayurveda research scales and seeks global scientific credibility.
Description:
The platform is a real-time, cloud-based Clinical Trial Management System (CTMS) and monitoring dashboard that gives AIIA a single, role-based, auditable view of its entire clinical-research portfolio.It tracks each study across its lifecycle - protocol and Institutional Ethics Committee approval, CTRI registration, site activation, screening, enrolment and randomization against target, visit and protocol-deviation compliance, data-query and data-quality status, study milestones and timelines, and close-out - surfaced as real-time Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) with configurable alerts (for example, enrolment lag, an ethics approval or CTRI update due, or an overdue monitoring visit).Because AIIA hosts the NPvCC, the dashboard integrates pharmacovigilance: it captures and routes Adverse Drug Reaction / Adverse-Event / Serious-Adverse-Event reports against regulatory reporting timelines, coded to standard dictionaries (MedDRA, WHODrug), and feeds aggregate safety signals to the Data Safety Monitoring Board and institutional leadership.Data must follow recognised clinical-research standards - CDISC (CDASH for data collection, SDTM for tabulation, ADaM for analysis) and HL7 FHIR R4 for interoperability with Electronic Data Capture (EDC), the hospital information system and Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM) building blocks - with full ALCOA+ data integrity and an immutable, time-stamped audit trail. Access is strictly role-based (Principal Investigator, study coordinator, monitor, Ethics Committee, pharmacovigilance, administration, and read-only regulator views).The platform must comply with GCP-ASU, the ICMR ethical guidelines, the NDCT Rules 2019 and CTRI requirements, and with the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 and its 2025 Rules - including informed-consent management, data minimisation, encryption, and hosting on compliant, data-resident cloud infrastructure secured to ISO/IEC 27001 and CERT-In norms, since clinical-trial data is sensitive personal data.
Expected solution:
A deployable, cloud-based CTMS-and-analytics dashboard providing: a real-time portfolio view with per-study drill-down; configurable KPIs and alerting; strictly role-based access and an immutable, ALCOA+-compliant audit trail; CDISC-aligned data models and HL7 FHIR R4 / ABDM interoperability with EDC and the hospital information system; an integrated pharmacovigilance module (AE/SAE capture, MedDRA/WHO Drug coding, regulatory-timeline tracking) reflecting AIIA’s NPvCC role; CTRI and ethics/regulatory milestone tracking; informed-consent and privacy controls aligned to the DPDP regime; electronic-signature and data-integrity controls consistent with GCP; and the ability to export submission-ready datasets (SDTM / ADaM, Define-XML). It should present tailored dashboards for Investigators, the Ethics Committee, pharmacovigilance and institutional leadership, and be hosted on secure, data-resident cloud infrastructure (ISO/IEC 27001, CERT-In). The build can be staged - a core study-tracking and KPI MVP first, then EDC/FHIR integration and the pharmacovigilance module, then full CDISC submission export and advanced analytics. The system should be evaluable on data accuracy and integrity, timeliness of safety and regulatory reporting, interoperability conformance, and access-control and audit completeness.
summary: Innovation (1/5): draws on standard software/hardware techniques applied to a space technology problem, placing it in the incremental band. Feasibility (2/5): as a software build with higher integration complexity, a full build is tight for 36 hours and will need scope-cutting. Impact (5/5): reaches a broad public/citizen base within Space Technology. Tech Depth (4/5): centers on integration, encryption, real-time. Sustainability (3/5): will need a maintenance/upkeep plan post-hackathon. Scalability (5/5): built to extend across states/users with modest rework. Total 20/30 -> Yellow verdict.

detail.title: AIIA Clinical Trials Dashboard - GCP-Compliant CTMS for Ayurveda Research

overview.in_plain_terms: Build a single dashboard that lets AIIA track every clinical trial in real time, recruitment, safety events, regulatory deadlines, instead of scattered spreadsheets that make compliance risk easy to miss.
overview.why_it_matters: Missed safety-reporting timelines or compliance gaps in clinical trials aren't just paperwork problems, they carry real regulatory and patient-safety consequences. A unified system directly reduces that risk.
pain_points: Study status, recruitment, and safety data tracked across disconnected spreadsheets.
No single, real-time, auditable view for AIIA's growing trial portfolio.
Risk of delayed decisions and missed regulatory reporting timelines.
overview.background: AIIA runs a growing portfolio of Ayurveda clinical trials under a demanding compliance framework (CTRI registration, GCP-ASU, NDCT Rules 2019, ethics oversight, adverse-event reporting), but currently tracks everything manually across disconnected tools.
overview.whats_being_asked: A real-time, cloud-based, GCP-compliant Clinical Trial Management System with CDISC/FHIR-interoperable data, role-based KPIs, and integrated ethics, regulatory, and pharmacovigilance tracking.
expected_solution: Real-time, role-based dashboard view of trial status, recruitment, and milestones.
Integrated regulatory/ethics/pharmacovigilance tracking with deadline alerts.

analysis.innovation_scope_note: Incremental as scored, CTMS platforms exist as an established category, though this specific compliance framework (GCP-ASU, CTRI, NDCT 2019) applied to Ayurveda trials is a narrower, more specialized application.
analysis.invention_effort_note: Moderate-high. Achieving genuine CDISC/FHIR interoperability and correctly modeling the specific regulatory reporting requirements is real, detailed engineering work, not a generic dashboard build.

competitive_landscape.note: Highly specialized clinical-trials compliance software, very few teams will have both the healthcare-data-standards knowledge and regulatory research appetite this requires.

innovation.note: CTMS platforms are an established category; value is domain-specific compliance modeling, not novel architecture.

invention.note: CDISC/FHIR interoperability and accurate regulatory-deadline logic require real technical and domain depth.

technical_feasibility.note: Genuine CDISC/FHIR compliance and accurate modeling of GCP-ASU/CTRI/NDCT requirements in 36 hours is ambitious, scope to core dashboard functionality plus one interoperability standard.

impact_and_benefits.note: Directly reduces compliance risk and speeds decision-making for a real, scaling national research programme.

architecture.note: Multiple data domains (recruitment, safety, regulatory, ethics) feeding one dashboard with real interoperability standards, genuine integration work.

overall_verdict.reasoning: Strong pick for a team with healthcare-data-standards knowledge specifically. Scope to a working dashboard with accurate regulatory-deadline logic and partial interoperability compliance, rather than claiming full CDISC/FHIR conformance you can't fully validate.

evaluator_lens.biggest_strength: Extremely well-specified regulatory framework named explicitly (CTRI, GCP-ASU, NDCT 2019), giving clear, concrete requirements to build against rather than vague compliance language.
evaluator_lens.biggest_risk: Claiming full CDISC/FHIR interoperability without genuine standards expertise risks a technically incorrect implementation that wouldn't actually interoperate with real systems.
evaluator_lens.validate_before_commit: Scope your interoperability claim honestly, implement core FHIR resource structures correctly for your demo's data rather than claiming broad CDISC/FHIR compliance you haven't fully validated.

idea_0_4: Research the specific regulatory reporting deadlines and requirements (CTRI, GCP-ASU, adverse-event timelines) to ground your deadline-tracking logic.
Choose one interoperability standard (FHIR is more broadly documented and tooled) to implement correctly rather than claiming both CDISC and FHIR.
Split: one person on the dashboard/KPI backend, one on regulatory-deadline and compliance-tracking logic.
prototype_4_22: Build the core trial-tracking dashboard: recruitment status, milestones, role-based views.
Build the regulatory/ethics/pharmacovigilance deadline-tracking and alerting logic.
Start FHIR-compliant data structuring for your core trial data model.
integration_22_30: Connect dashboard, deadline tracking, and data structure into one coherent system.
Test with a simulated overdue adverse-event report to confirm the alerting logic fires correctly.
Add role-based access views (researcher vs. ethics committee vs. regulatory officer).
polish_30_36: Polish the dashboard for a genuinely professional clinical-research-tool feel.
Rehearse explaining your specific regulatory-deadline logic and interoperability scope honestly.
Prepare to discuss how this would integrate with AIIA's actual multi-centre trial reality.
build_plan.how_to_stand_out: Simulate an approaching regulatory deadline (e.g. an adverse-event report due soon) live in the demo and show the system flag it before it's missed, that's the actual value proposition made tangible.

strengths: Extremely well-specified regulatory framework gives concrete, researchable requirements.
Real, systemic impact for a scaling national research programme.
weaknesses: Full CDISC/FHIR interoperability claims are hard to validate genuinely in 36 hours, must be scoped honestly.
Requires real healthcare-data-standards knowledge, not broadly accessible to a general software team.

team_fit.ideal_ratio: Weight toward regulatory research and data-standards knowledge, that's what separates this from a generic project-tracking dashboard.
team_fit.approach: Research the actual regulatory reporting timelines first, this grounds your deadline-tracking logic in real requirements rather than assumptions.

ai_buildability_split.ai_can_build_fast: The dashboard UI and standard project-tracking backend patterns.
ai_buildability_split.needs_human_judgment: Correctly implementing FHIR resource structures and accurately modeling the specific regulatory reporting deadlines, that requires real standards and domain knowledge, not assumed generic compliance logic.
ai_buildability_split.risk_of_leaning_on_ai_only: An AI-scaffolded 'compliant' system with incorrectly modeled regulatory deadlines could give false assurance that reporting obligations are being tracked when they aren't, a genuine risk in a clinical trial compliance context.

data_resource_availability.status: No real AIIA trial data is accessible; realistic sample trial data must be constructed based on the described regulatory framework.
data_resource_availability.backup_plan: Build sample trial data grounded in publicly available CTRI registration format and GCP-ASU guideline structure, clearly labeled as illustrative.

judge_qna.question: Is your system actually FHIR-compliant, or does it just use FHIR terminology?
judge_qna.strong_answer: Show your actual FHIR resource structure for a specific data type (e.g. adverse event reporting) and be honest about the scope of what you implemented versus full standard conformance.
judge_qna.follow_up: What would full CDISC compliance additionally require beyond what you built?

judge_qna.question: How did you determine the specific regulatory deadlines your system tracks?
judge_qna.strong_answer: Cite the specific guidelines you researched (GCP-ASU, NDCT 2019 timelines), don't present generic 'compliance tracking' as if it reflects the actual specific regulatory requirements without grounding.
judge_qna.follow_up: What happens when a regulation changes, how does the system stay current?
